sections.h2: Who bills and collects property tax in Wayne County
sections.html:
Your town tax collector sends out and collects the combined town and county bill. If it is still unpaid after March, the Wayne County Treasurer in Lyons takes over. The county has no cities. It has 15 towns and seven villages on the south shore of Lake Ontario, and Lyons is the county seat.

The county's Real Property Tax Services Agency works behind the scenes. It produces the assessment rolls, tax rolls and tax bills for the towns, villages and school districts, keeps the tax maps, investigates correction-of-error requests, divides the county levy among the assessing jurisdictions and calculates tax rates. It also supplies bills to 22 school districts, some of which lie outside the county.

  • Town tax collector: current Town and County bill, January through March.
  • County Treasurer, P.O. Box 8, Lyons, NY 14489, phone 315-946-7441: delinquent bills, installment agreements and the foreclosure auction.
  • Town assessor: value, exemption forms and ownership changes.
  • Real Property Tax Service page on the county site: assessment rolls, tax maps, rate documents and a parcel viewer.

sections.h2: Due dates and what waiting costs
sections.html:
Each town issues the Town and County bill around January 1, and you pay the town collector in January, February or March. Pay in January and nothing extra is added. Pay in February and 1 percent is added. Pay in March and 2 percent is added.

The tax year runs from January 1 to December 31. An owner can pay current taxes in two payments. The first falls due by the end of the penalty-free period, and the second is due in February or March with interest added. A buyer who closed after March 1 will not receive a bill until the next billing cycle, but the owner is still responsible for paying on time even when no bill arrives.

Rural fire, rural light and rural water or sewer charges can appear on a bill as special assessments, so a parcel in the countryside may carry lines that a village lot does not. Your bill is the taxable assessment multiplied by the rate, plus those special charges.

sections.h2: When Wayne County taxes go unpaid
sections.html:
On April 1 the town bill counts as delinquent and goes to the County Treasurer. The county can foreclose when taxes stay unpaid for two years. Costs pile up in steps once the Treasurer holds the bill.

  • April 1: the bill moves to the Treasurer, with a 25 percent penalty at transfer.
  • After receipt: a 5 percent penalty and 1 percent interest for each month the tax stays delinquent.
  • September of the second year: an enforcement fee of $450 or more is added, and the parcel is advertised in local papers for three non-consecutive weeks.
  • March, tentatively: the last chance to redeem before foreclosure, followed by a public auction of unpaid parcels in June.

The Treasurer runs a payment program for eligible owners. It is available for delinquent taxes after June 1, runs up to 24 months and needs a down payment of at least 10 percent. Call the office before any step above, because the payoff changes every month.

State law sets the outer frame. Under RPTL 1110 a delinquent lien can be redeemed by paying the amount due plus legal charges before the redemption period ends, normally two years after the lien date. A change to Article 11 in 2024 now returns surplus proceeds of a tax sale to the former owner. The Treasurer's office handles the sales.

sections.h2: Village and school taxes on the January bill
sections.html:
If you skip a village or school bill, the unpaid amount is added to the January Town and County bill with extra fees. Village taxes are paid to the village clerk from June 1 through October 31, and school taxes are paid to the school district from September 1 through October 31.

Anything still open on November 1 gets relevied. For a seller this means a January bill that looks too large may contain last fall's school or village balance. Ask the Treasurer or your town collector whether any relevy appears, and check the county site for the date a bill was paid.

sections.h2: How assessments are set and challenged
sections.html:
Your town assessor sets your assessment, and a local Board of Assessment Review hears complaints. Every town has a five-member board except Ontario, Savannah and Sodus, and Sodus moved to three members during 2024. Ask your town assessor when filing closes, since the date is set locally.

Owners of one-, two- and three-family owner-occupied homes can go on to a Small Claims Assessment Review hearing. Anyone may file a certiorari petition in Supreme Court. The county's policy, adopted by the Board of Supervisors in 1995, is that it joins a case only when the assessed value reaches $1,000,000. Clerical errors and similar mistakes can be corrected under RPTL 550 to 559.

Equalization rates show how far each town's roll sits from full market value. The county treats 100 percent as the goal because it means fewer correction, small claims and certiorari filings. Butler and Lyons were finishing a 2025 reassessment and Marion and Galen were planning one for 2026, so those towns' numbers may have moved.

sections.h2: Farm land and your tax bill
sections.html:
Working orchards and fields can qualify for an agricultural assessment, and Wayne County has a lot of it. About 174,632 of 295,113 acres in the agricultural district receive an exemption under Article 25-AA, and the county is the largest apple-producing county in New York.

If you sell a house with acreage, ask the town assessor whether the land carries an agricultural assessment and what a change of use would do. A buyer who plans to stop farming should hear about any change in assessment before the contract is signed.

The county had an estimated 91,250 residents in July 2025. Owners occupy 79.9 percent of homes, a high share, and the median owner-occupied home is valued at $170,000 for 2020 to 2024. Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,541, against $666 without one, and median gross rent is $938.

These are countywide medians, so a lake-view property in Sodus Point and a village house in Clyde can differ widely. Recent sales near your own address tell you more than any county figure.

sections.h2: Selling a Wayne County house with tax due
sections.html:
Get a written payoff from the right office for each layer of tax, because the town collector, the Treasurer, the village and the school district each hold different pieces. A short list keeps the closing on schedule.

  • Ask the town collector whether the current Town and County bill is paid, and how much interest applies to the month you close.
  • Call the Treasurer at 315-946-7441 if any bill went past April 1, and ask for the figure including penalties, interest and any enforcement fee.
  • Ask whether village or school balances were relevied onto the January bill.
  • Confirm with the town assessor that the owner name and any farm or senior exemption are correct.

The payoffs come out of the sale price at closing, so a cash buyer can still close while taxes are open. Order the payoff letters early, because interest is added each month and the figure moves with the closing date.

faqs.q: Who do I pay Wayne County property tax to?
faqs.a: Pay your town tax collector in January, February or March. After April 1 an unpaid bill goes to the Wayne County Treasurer's Office, P.O. Box 8, Lyons, NY 14489, phone 315-946-7441.

faqs.q: Does Wayne County offer a payment plan for back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, for eligible owners. The program covers delinquent taxes after June 1, runs up to 24 months and needs a down payment of at least 10 percent. Call the Treasurer to find out whether you qualify.

faqs.q: How long before Wayne County can foreclose?
faqs.a: Two years of unpaid taxes. The public auction usually falls in June, and the tentative last redemption date is in March.

faqs.q: What if I bought a house after March 1 in Wayne County?
faqs.a: You will not get a bill until the next billing cycle, but you are still responsible for paying on time. Ask the town tax collector for the amount before the penalty-free period ends.

faqs.q: Where do I look up my Wayne County assessment and tax maps?
faqs.a: Use the Real Property Tax Service page on the Wayne County website. It links to assessment rolls, tax maps, tax rate documents and a GIS parcel viewer, and your town assessor can answer questions about your parcel.
